generic_sampling_rules.integer_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; generated ids are offset past the compact max so they never collide with compact rows.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_foreign_key: Sample from the final (post-offset) parent primary-key values; never NULL (all FK columns are NOT NULL here).
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from the observed value pool for the column; with probability 0.15 emit a near-variant (case change, trailing space, or one-character edit) of a pool value; never NULL unless the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_nullable: With probability equal to the compact database's null share (0.0 here, so at least one NULL row per nullable column is still planted per instruction 10), emit NULL; otherwise sample from the observed pool with 0.15 near-variant probability.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_measure: Sample integers within the observed min/max of the column; include boundary values (min, min+1, max-1, max) at least once. Coerce any near-variant string via int(float(str(v).strip())) with try/except fallback to a random positive integer; never raise.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_text: Sample uniformly from the observed distinct values of the column.

targets.note: At least one enzyme.name starts with 'ALA' (e.g. 'ALA synthase') and at least one contains 'ALA' not at the start, so both LIKE patterns match distinct rows.
At least one enzyme row whose id never appears in medicine_enzyme_interaction.enzyme_id.
At least one enzyme id appears in >=2 interaction rows and at least one in exactly 1, so COUNT(DISTINCT) > 1 and = 1 both occur.

enzyme.id is a primary key so it is unique; the duplicate share applies to the join column medicine_enzyme_interaction.enzyme_id, which must repeat some enzyme ids so COUNT(DISTINCT enzyme.id) < COUNT(*).
At least one medicine row whose id never appears in medicine_enzyme_interaction.medicine_id.

Relaxed from [1,2,3,4] to [1,2,3] per review: with 19 interaction rows and 8 enzymes, a medicine group of size exactly 4 is not guaranteed. Ensure medicine ids appear in interaction groups of size 1, 2, and >=3 so HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 and >= 3 both select and reject rows.
Grouping medicine.id by interaction count must yield groups of size 1, 2, and >=3.

medicine.name is unique per row, so grouping by name yields only size-1 groups; the size-2 and >=3 groups are produced by grouping medicine.name after joining to interactions (a medicine with multiple interactions).
After joining to interactions, at least one medicine.name group has COUNT(*) >= 2 and at least one has COUNT(*) = 1.
medicine.name values must be distinct enough that ORDER BY name ASC is deterministic; no ties required since no LIMIT is used.
Trade_Name is unique per row; size-2 and >=3 groups arise only after joining to interactions. Ensure at least one trade name maps to a medicine with >=3 interactions and one with exactly 2.
After joining, at least one Trade_Name group has COUNT(*) >= 3.
Ensure enzyme_id groups with COUNT = 1, 2, and >=3 so HAVING COUNT(enzyme_id) > 1 and >= 3 both select and reject.
At least one enzyme has no interaction rows (see enzyme.id exception).
At least one medicine has no interaction rows (see medicine.id exception).

Store canonical lowercase 'activitor' and 'inhibitor' so IN ('activitor','inhibitor') matches; both values must occur so COUNT(DISTINCT interaction_type) = 2 and each SUM(CASE ...) > 0. NULL planting must never remove the last non-NULL occurrence of either value.

aggregate: SUM(CASE WHEN interaction_type = 'activitor' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
SUM(CASE WHEN interaction_type = 'inhibitor' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
targets.note: Both interaction types must appear at least once so COUNT(DISTINCT) = 2 and both conditional sums are > 0. NULL planting is rule-aware: plant NULL only on a row whose type is duplicated, never on the last occurrence of a required enum value.

dependencies.note: FK; child enzyme_id must reference an existing enzyme.id. Parent rows without children are allowed (see exceptions). Plan interactions against the final post-offset parent ids.
FK; child medicine_id must reference an existing medicine.id. Parent rows without children are allowed (see exceptions). Plan interactions against the final post-offset parent ids.
Composite primary key; no duplicate (enzyme_id, medicine_id) pairs.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: All observed OMIM values are positive integers (125290, 125270, 176000, 606938, 176100, 121300, 600923, 177000).

supporting_evidence.enzyme.name_like: enzyme.name row 1 'ALA synthase' matches 'ALA%' and '%ALA%'; a second row containing 'ALA' not at start is needed for the '%ALA%' variant to differ.
supporting_evidence.enzyme.id_unmatched: enzyme has 8 rows but medicine_enzyme_interaction.enzyme_id has only 6 distinct values, so at least 2 enzymes have no children.
supporting_evidence.medicine.id_unmatched: medicine has 21 rows but medicine_enzyme_interaction.medicine_id has only 13 distinct values, so at least 8 medicines have no children.
supporting_evidence.interaction_type_enum: Observed values 'inhibitor' and 'activitor' (note the misspelling 'activitor' is canonical).
supporting_evidence.OMIM_positive: All 8 observed OMIM values are positive integers.

uncertainty: The duplicate_share 20-50% for enzyme.id cannot apply to the primary key itself; it is interpreted as applying to the join column medicine_enzyme_interaction.enzyme_id, which must repeat enzyme ids.
Group-size targets for medicine.name and medicine.Trade_Name (size 2 and >=3) are only achievable after joining to interactions, since both columns are unique per medicine row.

The 'activitor' spelling is preserved as canonical per the observed data; near-variants 'ACTIVITOR'/'INHIBITOR' are listed as comparison-boundary targets but the stored values should remain the canonical lowercase forms so IN predicates match.

Null shares are 0.0 in the compact database, but instruction 10 requires at least one NULL row per nullable column; this conflicts with the observed 0.0 share and is resolved in favor of instruction 10.
medicine.id aggregate_boundary relaxed from [1,2,3,4] to [1,2,3] per review: with 19 interaction rows and 8 enzymes, a medicine group of size exactly 4 is not guaranteed by the planner.
OMIM sampling must coerce near-variant strings via int(float(str(v).strip())) with try/except fallback to a random positive integer, so the POSITIVE rule never raises ValueError.
NULL planting for interaction_type must be rule-aware: plant NULL only on a row whose type is duplicated, never on the last non-NULL occurrence of 'activitor' or 'inhibitor'.

table_sizes_per_instance refers to the number of generated (appended) rows per instance, not the total instance size; the program appends these to the compact database, so the final instance has compact rows plus generated rows. All aggregate-boundary, group-size, unmatched-join and duplicate-share targets must be evaluated against the final compact+generated tables, and the program must plan interactions against the final post-offset parent ids and enable foreign-key enforcement (or run a post-insert FK check) so FK violations are caught rather than silently written.

The program must not silently skip interaction rows that are required to satisfy the specification; after writing, it must assert that the planned group sizes (enzyme_id groups 1/2/>=3, medicine_id groups 1/2/>=3), both interaction types, the unmatched-join targets and the duplicate share in [0.2,0.5] hold in the final instance, and report the achieved values.
